headline: Hike odds went 40% to 70% in a week, and Tuesday the 2-year finally traded like it. Payrolls Friday is the counterweight.
stance: Sep 16 FOMC hike pricing has roughly doubled in a week and the 2-year moved Tuesday to match. The supply steepener the long end built through August is now flattening from the front.

news.head: September hike goes from coin flip to base case
news.body: Odds for the Sep 16 FOMC ran near 70% this morning, from 40% a week ago. No Fed speaker did that. Oil and a 3.3% euro-area August print did.

news.head: Tankers struck in Hormuz, and then oil stopped
news.body: WTI $90.22 and Brent $94.85 overnight (~6am ET), both unchanged on the day. The gap is in the price and nothing is extending it before the open.

news.head: Gold gives back a fourth straight session
news.body: $4,304, -0.6% (~6am ET), near its lowest in three weeks. Four sessions of selling into a rising-rate bid, with gold vol barely up alongside it.

news.head: Hiring rate fell while openings held
news.body: July hires 3.2%, from 3.4%. Openings 7.27m against 7.30m expected. July payrolls were -23k. Friday's jobs report is the release that argues against a hike.

implications: The steepener and the hike are opposite trades. If the front end keeps repricing, 2s10s flattens from here and August's supply steepener stops paying.
A hike near 70% priced into a negative July payroll number is the whole risk. Friday's jobs report decides more of this month's meeting than anything else.

watch.head: Factory orders, 10:00
watch.body: The only release today. Low tier, but it is the hard-data check after August's factory survey slipped from July.

watch.head: ISM services, Thursday 10:00
watch.body: The half of the survey that has been holding up. With a hike priced, a strong number now reads hawkish rather than good.

watch.head: Jobs report, Friday 8:30
watch.body: Payrolls went negative in July and the hiring rate just fell again. This is the release that can take this month's meeting back off the table.

watch.head: Oil vol, not the oil price
watch.body: Crude vol rose to 49 on Tuesday alongside the level. Vol rising with price is the market adding supply risk, not fading it.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: The repricing moved to the front end Tuesday. That is a Fed trade, and it flattens the curve the long end spent August steepening.
10-year breakevens did the work, not real yields. The bond market is taking the oil move as inflation rather than as demand destruction.
Rate vol rose a third straight session. This time the yield moved with it; Monday it did not. That makes it a level move, not a hedge.
sections.positioning: Spec length in corn, wheat and soybeans all jumped last week, corn to a three-year maximum. Grains are positioned like oil now, and breakevens are pricing both.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Breadth fell a fourth straight session and the share of S&P names above their 50-day is now under half. The index moves have been smaller than that.
The Nasdaq's 200-day count fell seven points Tuesday. Nasdaq breadth is now weaker than the S&P's on both the 50- and the 200-day.
Nasdaq vol rose more than S&P vol Tuesday. Protection is being bought against the concentration rather than against the index.
sections.positioning: Spec positioning in VIX futures has sat at the 9th percentile of three years for three weeks. A standing extended short in vol, going into a meeting the market now expects to be live.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: The cash spread marks caught up through Monday and widened. Both the investment-grade and the high-yield marks gave back part of last week's tights.
HYG/LQD fell a fifth straight session. It has led the cash marks the whole way, so the widening in the marks is probably not finished.
Month-end came and went in a single session. The facility spiked Monday, emptied Tuesday, and funding spreads barely moved.
sections.positioning: Primary-dealer investment-grade inventory sits mid-range at the 56th percentile of three years, against the 6th in high yield. Dealers carry spread risk in one place only.
